rationale: A source does not become metadata merely because a desired field inside it is high-level classification data.
Regulator-hosted filed product documents may contain allowed classification fields adjacent to target or other semantic content.

Admitting a policy/prospectus/CIS-like document and filtering forbidden content after parsing would weaken the artifact-class firewall and make blindness depend on parser restraint rather than source-boundary structure.

Preselection classification evidence is admissible only when exposed through a regulator- or insurer-controlled metadata artifact, filing record, registry row, or structurally isolated filing cover sheet whose allowed field set is bounded by construction before selector exposure.

Machine acquisition of a forbidden semantic-bearing artifact for the purpose of extracting only selected classification fields remains forbidden during blind preselection unless a future architecture decision explicitly changes the artifact-class boundary.

supports: some product-type labels such as Individual, Group, Retail, Add On
irdai_health_product_register.limitation: Type Of Product is historically heterogeneous and cannot be treated as a universally complete taxonomy field.

regulator_hosted_filed_product_documents.reason: The same document/table may expose waiting-period, benefit, eligibility, coverage or other semantic content adjacent to classification fields.

blindness_rule.principle: Allowed classification evidence must be bounded by source structure before selector projection, not discovered by reading a semantic-bearing document and discarding forbidden content afterwards.

next_question: Do authoritative regulator/insurer metadata artifacts, filing records, structured indexes, or structurally isolated cover sheets expose the remaining necessary classification predicates without opening a semantic-bearing product document?
